artboards.title: HUD Plans tab — today (why it fights you)
Option C — Split list + live detail

annotations.text:
WHERE IT LIVES — any option can ride any of 3 integration routes:
1) an expand button on the op-chat Plans face → full-width takeover of the app pane
2) a new view of the /adv Plans tab (?view=mission) beside the existing list/editor
3) a new top-level /adv tab.
All four options reuse feeds that already exist: plans.list, advRoster.list, plans.attention, planSessions.list — "Open session" is the existing SessionChatModal. A and C compose naturally: A's table with C's detail as the expanded row.

OPTION A — Mission-control table (leading candidate). One dense row per plan: progress, live agents, ✎ last edit / ⚒ last work, needs-you. Click a row → inline expand with that plan's agent sessions + launch/transcript actions.
+ Cheapest full-width build; ~466 plans virtualized; sortable by any column (incl. last work).
− Least visual grouping; one plan expanded at a time.

OPTION B — Status board. Kanban by lifecycle bucket (draft / ready / running / finished); cards carry agent chips, both timestamps, progress strip.
+ Best pipeline overview — how much is in flight vs parked; drag-to-bucket later.
− Weaker for "who is working right now" scanning; long columns need collapse/virtualization at this plan count.

OPTION C — Split: list + live detail. Left = the Plans-face rows (with the dual times); right = always-on detail for the selected plan: working-now session cards + a merged edit/work activity feed.
+ Zero-modal drill-in — sessions and activity are one click, no popup.
− One plan's detail at a time; less of an all-plans overview than A.

OPTION D — Activity swimlanes. Time on x, one lane per active plan, bars = agent sessions (click → transcript). Stalls and overlap are visible at a glance — red now-line, amber stall flags.
− Highest build cost: needs a session-activity-interval feed (adv_sessions + tool_invocations time buckets) that doesn't exist yet. Best shipped later as a second view beside A/B/C.

ASK 1 — dual timestamps on the Plans-face row (PlansPane.tsx).
✎ last edit = harness_plans.updated — already on the row today.
⚒ last work = newest work-item activity where source_plan_slug = plan → one small new sync query (planWorkActivity.list: slug → timestamp), joined client-side exactly like the existing needs-you / live-agents maps.
V1 keeps the compact header pair; V2 spells it out in the status line. Hover = full timestamp + what happened. "stale" switches to max(edit, work) so a worked-but-unedited plan stops reading stale.

WHY THE HUD PLANS BOARD FIGHTS YOU — diagnosis from the actual code (HudEntityColumns.tsx, hud-entity-board.ts, hud.css):
1) FIVE EQUAL COLUMNS (repeat(5, minmax(190px,1fr))) — "Done" (hundreds of plans) gets the same width as "Needs you" (3). The width goes to the columns you never read; titles truncate at ~275px.
2) THE JOIN IS MISSING — plan cards carry no agents; sessions live in a different tab. "Who is working this plan right now?" = tab-hop + reading two boards. (The code even keeps the session model and entity model as deliberate siblings.)
3) NAVIGATION = THE FILTER BOX — columns cap at 60 cards, then "+N more — narrow with the filter". No sort, no grouping, no recency order you can see; the code's own comment: "without [search] the board is a wall".
4) WEAK HIERARCHY — identical card silhouettes, one ambiguous age number per card, 5 separate scrollbars; the count chips at top ARE filter buttons but read as statistics.
5) DRILL-IN COSTS YOUR PLACE — a card opens PlanPopupModal over the whole board.
Each fix below attacks these differently; all keep the HUD's data feeds (advRoster.list, plans.list, plans.attention) — this is presentation-layer surgery, not a data rebuild.

H1 — ATTENTION BANDS (board → banded list). Kills the columns: full-width rows under three loud bands (Needs you / In motion / Blocked); Ready + Done fold into one-line bars. Agents, dual times, and the ask sit ON the row; asks are answerable inline.
+ Fixes 1, 2, 3, 4 at once; one scrollbar; the eye path is top-to-bottom priority order.
− Loses the side-by-side "pipeline" gestalt; biggest visual change of the three.

H2 — WEIGHTED BOARD (conservative — keeps the kanban). Same five columns, but width follows attention: Needs-you and Working wide with rich cards (agents + ✎/⚒ times + who-is-doing-what line), Blocked narrow, Ready/Done collapse to count rails that expand on click. Count chips become a real labeled filter strip; a sort picker appears.
+ Smallest change that fixes 1, 2 and half of 4; the board stays recognizably the board.
− Filter box is still the only deep navigation (3); drill-in still a modal (5).

H3 — UNIFIED ACTIVITY LANES (merge the tabs). The tab axis (goals/sessions/plans/items) becomes a FILTER; one board where the plan (or goal) is a full-width lane holding its own live sessions, its answerable asks, and its dual times. Solo sessions group in a lane of their own. Quiet/blocked lanes collapse to a header row.
+ Fixes all five — especially 2: the plan↔agent join IS the layout. The strongest "what is happening?" surface.
− Biggest build + a real information-architecture change (needs the goals/sessions boards to fold in); overlaps most with the separate plans dashboard — if H3 lands, mission-control option A/C may be redundant (and vice versa). Decide them together.
